title: Fuzzy team resolution silently maps unknown teams to unrelated clubs
evidence: soccer_mcp/queries.py:45-47 — difflib.get_close_matches(cutoff=0.6) with no ambiguity check. Verified: _resolve_team(store,'Real Madrid') -> 'real garcilaso'; _resolve_team(store,'Atletico') -> 'atletico es' (not Atletico Mineiro/Paranaense); _resolve_team(store,'America') -> 'americano'. Every team-scoped tool (search_matches, team_stats, head_to_head, biggest_wins) then returns confidently wrong data instead of the QueryError on line 48.
suggestion: Raise QueryError when the best match's ratio is below a stricter cutoff (~0.85), or when the top-2 candidates are within a small delta, and return the candidate list as a disambiguation prompt.

title: standings() declares a champion and relegation zone without checking the season is complete
evidence: soccer_mcp/queries.py:517-520 unconditionally sets rows[0]['champion']=True and rows[-4:]['relegated']=True for any serie a season. The 2023 Serie A source (BR-Football-Dataset.csv, 377 of 380 rows — verified raw) leaves Palmeiras and Red Bull Bragantino on 37 played, so standings(store,2023,'serie a') reports Gremio champion (68 pts, 38 played) ahead of Palmeiras (67 pts, 37 played) — Palmeiras were the actual 2023 champions.
suggestion: Only set champion/relegated when every team has played the same, expected number of matches; otherwise emit a 'season incomplete (N/M matches)' warning in the result.

title: requirements.txt omits every test dependency
evidence: requirements.txt:1-3 lists only pandas>=2.0, fastmcp>=2.10, mcp>=1.8, but tests/conftest.py:12 imports pytest_bdd, pytest.ini:4 declares an asyncio marker (pytest-asyncio) and coverage was collected (.coverage). A clean `pip install -r requirements.txt` cannot run the suite.
suggestion: Add a requirements-dev.txt (or a [project.optional-dependencies] test extra) pinning pytest, pytest-bdd, pytest-asyncio and coverage.

title: 14 E501 line-too-long violations (>88 cols)
evidence: ruff check --select E,F,W: e.g. soccer_mcp/data.py:359:89 (97 cols), soccer_mcp/queries.py:294:89 (99 cols), soccer_mcp/queries.py:346:89 (91 cols). This is the whole reason code_quality scored 0.6667 — 21 diagnostics drive the scorer's lint component to 0.0 (retort.db code_quality=0.6667 = (0.0 lint + 1.0 structure + 1.0 stderr)/3).
suggestion: Run `ruff format` / wrap the offending lines; no functional change.

title: 7 F401 unused imports, all in tests
evidence: tests/test_mcp_server.py:11,15,16,17 (head_to_head, search_players, standings, team_stats); tests/bdd/test_match_queries.py:5,6 (pytest, pytest_bdd.given); tests/conftest.py:12 (pytest_bdd.when).
suggestion: Delete the unused imports (ruff --fix handles all seven).

title: standings() builds a league table for knockout competitions
evidence: soccer_mcp/queries.py:469 accepts any competition _resolve_competition() knows. standings(store,2022,'copa libertadores') returns a 32-team 'table' from 120 matches with unequal fixtures — Flamengo 12 played/34 pts ranked above Estudiantes 10 played/18 pts — which is not a meaningful standing.
suggestion: Restrict standings() to league competitions (serie a/b/c) and raise QueryError with a pointer to head_to_head/search_matches for cup competitions.
